capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company initiated a modernisation programme across its spinning operations, replacing older-generation ring frames at the Amravati unit with advanced next-generation systems equipped with linked auto-coners, which increased spindle capacity at the Amravati facility. At the Ramtek denim division, the Company installed a next-generation Autocoro 10 machine with individual drive technology to strengthen spinning capabilities and support a broader range of specialised yarn production.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- integration: Integrated manufacturing operations across yarn and denim fabric manufacturing enabling greater control over quality, production efficiency and supply chain management — evidence: presence across yarn and denim fabric manufacturing, evidenced by spinning, processing and fabric manufacturing operations at facilities in Telangana and Maharashtra.
- customer lock-in: Long-standing relationships with leading global brands as an Original Denim Manufacturer — evidence: continues to secure continued business from existing global brands such as Walmart, Levi's, Wrangler, Lee and Kontoor.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Fluctuations in cotton prices and input costs continue to affect cost structures and margins across the textile value chain; variability in domestic cotton supply has led to firm input prices, creating cost pressures across the value chain.
- Competition from lower-cost manufacturing countries and duty-related factors in export markets affect price competitiveness; elevated import duties in key export markets continue to affect competitiveness, prompting some manufacturers to consider alternative production locations. US tariff-related issues adversely impacted the business as several US brands reduced order volumes and postponed buying decisions.
- The West Asia conflict from late February 2026 onwards affected global market sentiment and created uncertainties in international trade which are still not resolved.
- Compliance with water management and effluent treatment requirements involves ongoing capital and operating expenditure; stringent sustainability and traceability requirements in developed markets are increasing compliance costs, particularly for smaller enterprises.
- The fragmented unorganised sector continues to account for a large share of volumes, competing on price and affecting margin stability for organised players.
- Higher energy, logistics and production costs compared to competing countries continue to affect margins.
- Geographical dispersion across spinning, processing and garmenting operations continues to increase logistics costs and lead times.
